title: 2007 AMC 12A Problem 21
statement: The sum of the zeros, the product of the zeros, and the sum of the coefficients of the function \(f(x)=ax^2+bx+c\) are equal. Their common value must also be which of the following?

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text: one of the \(x\)-intercepts of the graph of \(y=f(x)\)

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
the mean of the \(x\)-intercepts of the graph of
\(y=f(x)\)

solutions.text:
The product of the zeros is \(\tfrac ca\) and the sum of the zeros is \(-\tfrac ba.\) Equating them gives \(c=-b.\)

Then the sum of the coefficients is \(a+b+c=a,\) which is the coefficient of \(x^2.\)

The other choices fail in general: for \(f(x)=-2x^2-4x+4\) the common value is \(-2,\) but the coefficient of \(x\) is \(-4,\) the \(y\)-intercept is \(4,\) the \(x\)-intercepts are \(-1\pm\sqrt3,\) and their mean is \(-1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: For \(ax^2+bx+c,\) the sum of zeros is \(-\tfrac ba\) and the product is \(\tfrac ca\)
Setting these equal gives \(c=-b,\) so the sum of coefficients \(a+b+c\) simplifies
